anti_patterns: Deploying with no mass-exit path: a data-withholding operator forces users to dump the entire last-valid state onto L1 at once, congesting the root chain beyond its processing capacity
Exiting on unfinalized or unincluded state: starting standard exits from transactions never included in a committed block, which any observer can challenge and which forfeits the exit bond

Single-operator chain with no watcher coverage: a Proof-of-Authority operator plus zero independent watchers voids the one-honest-observer assumption, leaving invalid blocks and double-spend exits unchallenged
Running general smart-contract computation on Plasma: the UTXO / coin-slot model (MoreVP allows 4 inputs and 4 outputs per transaction) cannot express arbitrary EVM logic, unlike rollups
Treating operator preconfirmations as final: building irreversible L1 actions on uncommitted child-chain output instead of waiting for the root-anchored commitment and challenge window
Ignoring in-flight transactions at operator failure: covering only included UTXOs while broadcast-but-unincluded transfers have no in-flight exit route and become unrecoverable
avoid_when: The application needs general-purpose EVM computation or composable smart contracts: Plasma supports payments and simple transfers, not arbitrary logic
Withdrawals need L1 finality in minutes: every exit must survive a challenge window (minimum exit period of about 7 days in the OMG MoreVP deployment)
No party will run a watcher or monitor exit games: safety depends on at least one online, funded observer per challenge period
Strict data-residency or permissioning rules forbid operator-held off-chain transaction data outside user-controlled stores
benefits: Throughput decoupled from L1: only Merkle block roots touch the root chain in the happy path, so the child chain confirms at operator speed (thousands of TPS class) instead of 15-30 TPS
Minimal L1 fees: users pay L1 gas only for deposits, exits, and periodic commitments, not per payment
Root-chain settlement without custodial trust: assets are locked in the root contract and a single honest observer can defeat fraud, so users never entrust funds to the operator
Unilateral exit: any user can withdraw against the last valid commitment even when the operator turns malicious or withholds blocks
Hierarchical nesting: child chains can themselves parent further chains, pushing settlement down the tree and only touching the root on dispute or exit
Light client proofs: Plasma Cash coin slots with Sparse Merkle Trees let users verify only the branches covering their own coins instead of downloading the whole child chain
best_practices: Run at least one independent watcher from day one, validating the child chain at least once per challenge half-period, with bonded capital and gas budgets sized for an attack
Set the minimum finalization period to about 7 days split into two halves (challenges in the first, responses in the second) so honest users always have time to respond
Require exit bonds on every exit and piggyback so successful challengers are compensated and spam exits are priced out
Support both standard exits (for included UTXOs) and in-flight exits (for broadcast-but-unincluded transfers) so operator block withholding strands no honest user
Consolidate UTXOs before exiting: each coin slot exits separately, so fewer, larger UTXOs mean fewer L1 exit transactions
Quarantine newly registered exit games and vaults (default three times the minimum exit period) so users can audit new adjudication logic before it governs their funds
component_types: Root Contract (PlasmaFramework): L1 contract holding deposits in token vaults, recording committed child-chain block roots, and running the exit queue with priority ordering
Child-Chain Operator: off-chain block producer (Proof-of-Authority single operator in the OMG deployment) ordering UTXO transfers and publishing Merkle roots to the root contract
Watcher Network: distributed observers verifying child-chain blocks, alerting users to Byzantine behavior, and submitting spent-coin, before-deposit, and invalid-history challenges
Exit Game Contracts (PaymentExitGame): adjudicate the challenge-response protocol, verify inclusion and non-inclusion proofs, and slash bonds on fraud
Token Vaults: ETH and ERC-20 escrow contracts backing every child-chain balance 1:1 with locked L1 collateral
context: Ethereum L1 settles only 15-30 TPS with volatile gas fees, pricing out high-volume payments while remaining the most secure settlement layer available. Plasma moves execution onto a hierarchical child chain anchored to the root chain: users deposit ETH or ERC-20s into a root contract and transact off-chain at operator speed, while the operator periodically commits only Merkle block roots to L1. Because the root chain cannot verify off-chain data, correctness is enforced optimistically: anyone observing an invalid transition submits a fraud proof to the root contract inside a challenge window (about 7 days), and exits are priority-ordered by coin age so a malicious operator cannot front-run honest withdrawals. Variants refine the model: Plasma MVP defines the UTXO exit game, MoreVP removes confirmation signatures via standard plus in-flight exits, and Plasma Cash assigns non-fungible coin slots with Sparse Merkle Trees for light proofs. When the operator withholds data, users fall back to mass exit against the last valid commitment.
design_principles: Commit hashes, keep data off-chain: only Merkle roots anchor to L1 in the happy path; full transaction data stays with the operator
Unilateral exitability: every honest user must be able to recover funds from the last valid commitment with no operator cooperation
Optimistic acceptance with bonded challenges: accept exits by default, let any observer cancel fraud inside the dispute window, and slash the liar's bond
Priority-ordered exits: oldest coins exit first so attackers cannot race honest users during a mass exit
One-honest-observer sufficiency: a single vigilant watcher must be able to protect all users, mirroring the 1-of-N assumption of optimistic systems

technology_stack: OMG PlasmaFramework root contracts (PlasmaFramework, PaymentExitGame, ETH and ERC-20 vaults)
elixir-omg child chain and watcher services (Tesuji design, Proof-of-Authority operator)
MoreVP exit protocol (standard exits plus in-flight exits, exit and piggyback bonds)
Plasma Cash Sparse Merkle Tree coin-slot contracts (PlasmaChain.vy, PlasmaRegistry.vy)
UTXO payment transaction type with 4 inputs and 4 outputs per child-chain transaction
tradeoffs: Slow withdrawals: every exit waits out the challenge window (about 7 days minimum), so Plasma cannot serve use cases needing fast L1 finality
Data-availability dependence: transaction data lives with the operator, so block withholding blinds challengers and forces a mass exit that dumps the full last-valid state onto L1 at once
User liveness burden: holders must watch the chain (directly or via a watcher service) at least once per challenge period or risk losing funds to unchallenged fraud
No general computation: the UTXO and coin-slot models express payments and simple transfers only, unlike EVM-equivalent rollups
Operator centralization in practice: production deployments run a single Proof-of-Authority operator, so short-term liveness and ordering depend on one party plus the exit hatch
Exit complexity and cost: each UTXO exits separately with bonds and proofs (spent-coin, before-deposit, invalid-history challenges), making many-small-coin wallets expensive to rescue
use_cases: High-volume micropayments and retail transfers settling to Ethereum without per-payment L1 gas (OMG Network production deployment)
Gaming and consumer-app token economies needing operator-speed confirmations with root-chain-backed balances
Non-fungible and range-based asset transfers using Plasma Cash coin slots with light proofs for the holder's own coins
Hierarchical settlement networks where regional child chains net internally and only disputes or exits reach the root chain
